LESSON: KENYAN FOLK DANCE

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five
Subject: WITH HEARIG IMPAIRMENT CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Performing and Displaying
Topic 2.3: Kenyan Folk Dance
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 18

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Kenyan Folk Dance, part of Performing and Displaying in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five WITH HEARIG IMPAIRMENT CREATIVE ARTS.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to perform a folk dance? 2. What is the role of costumes, body adornment and ornaments in a dance?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Kenyan Folk Dance together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: Learners communicate their ideas, feelings and emotions during dancing.

● Creativity and Imagination: Learners create various formations and patterns in during folk dance.

● Citizenship: Enhanced during performance of folk dances from Kenya diverse communities.

Values:
● Unity: This is developed when performing folk dances from other communities as learners relate and interact with each

other.

● Responsibility: is inculcated through taking different roles in a dance as well as maintaining discipline in group

relationships.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Safety and security: Learners take precaution when handling different tools and materials in making the costume and

ornament for use in a folk-dance performance.

● Environmental issues: Learners source/ improve costumes and props using recycled resources from the local environment.

Link to other learning areas

Indigenous languages- Performing different folk songs and dances from different ethnic groups..

Suggested learning resources.

Sisal skirts, percussion instruments, whistles, flags, whiskers.
